Congresswoman Bets on Musk & Buffett
Rep.
Maria Elvira Salazar
(R-Fla.) recently disclosed multiple stock transactions from August, as reported by the
The trades included multiple sales of stocks like
IBM

. The transactions also included several buys.
Salazar disclosed buying $1,000 to $15,000 in
Space Exploration Technologies Corp
) on two different occasions on Aug. 12.
Unlike

who bought SpaceX stock around the time of the IPO, Salazar may have timed her trades better, with shares of the space company trading between $134.01 and $149.60 on Aug. 12 and trading at $148.18 now.
The purchase of SpaceX stock could show a belief in CEO Musk and his future space visions for the Moon and Mars.
Along with betting on Musk, Salazar is also betting on the success of stocks picked by Buffett.
Salazar disclosed buying
Berkshire Hathaway B

(NYSE:BRK) shares on Aug. 7 with a purchase of $1,000 to $15,000 in shares. This purchase follows the congresswoman also buying Berkshire stock back in July in increments of $1,000 to $15,000 and $15,000 to $50,000.
While Buffett stepped down as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway at the end of 2025, many of the top holdings, and even recent bets on Alphabet, are picks made by Buffett himself.
The congresswoman could be betting on the continued success of Buffett’s old picks and/or the new picks of new CEO
Greg Abel.
Outside of betting on Musk and Abel, the other trades that stand out are buying shares of
Merck & Co. Inc
(NYSE:MRK) and
Moderna Inc
(NASDAQ:MRNA).
Shares of Merck and Moderna were both purchased on Aug. 19, the day Moderna shared news of the successful Phase 3 melanoma cancer vaccine that uses Merck’s Keytruda.
Moderna stock was highly volatile on that day, trading in a range of $114.46 to $176.66.
Salazar bought Moderna stock on Aug. 19 and also sold shares on the same day, according to the disclosure.
The Merck shares have not been sold.

Salazar’s Trading History
The congresswoman has made over 120 trades since 2022, totaling $8.67 million, according to data from Quiver Quantitative.
Salazar made zero transactions in 2025, according to Quiver Quantitative, which came after trading more than $2.3 million in 2024.
The congresswoman is already over $1.55 million in trades for 2026, with $1.33 million in purchases and $218,000 in sales.
Salazar currently sits on the House Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Financial Services Committee. She also serves on subcommittees for housing, capital markets and national security.
Those committee assignments could put her stock purchase, like some made previously, under more attention from retail investors.
